items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Master's degree in relevant field.
Juris Doctorate (JD) Degree strongly preferred.
3 - 5 years of related experience.
Experience working in diverse educational contexts including HSI, AANAPISI.
Experience working with diverse constituencies.
Experience in legal education or practice.
Provides advice and assistance to students on all aspects of their academic experience, including progression and requirement matters for the department/school/college. (15% time)
Advises new and continuing instructors on student advising issues. (15% time)
Advises on special eligibility requirements such as Honors programs/fellowships/scholarships. (10% time)

Participates in planning academic curriculum in collaboration with chair/dean and faculty, and with other departments, to ensure student's progress through course sequences, avoid conflicts, and ensure compliance with organization-wide policies. (10% time)

Determines barriers, distractions, and complications affecting a student's academic success, helps students recognize these key non-academic issues, and makes appropriate referrals for additional therapeutic counseling and/or assistance from other units. (10% time)

Educate students about the variety of career opportunities in the legal professions, and the different types of available (i.e. Juris Doctorate, Master of Laws, Paralegal Studies). Advise students in course selection specific to the preparation for law school, the legal profession and criminal justice system writ large. Advise students in the Law School Admissions Council (LSAC) application process—including available modes of preparing for the Law School Admissions Test (LSAT)—and assist students in gaining admission to appropriate law schools. (5% time)

Disseminate information to students, advisors, faculty and others, including: creation of pre-law resources print and electronic information about the legal profession, law school application timetables, information about the LSAT exam, schedules for on- and off- campus events, etc.; as well as the development and maintenance of pre-law advising information on the PPAC website. (5% time)

Actively engage with faculty across all colleges/schools in support of pre-law students and activities; encourage course development on topics related to the legal profession with specific correlation to the Law & Society Program. Actively engage and collaborate with advisors and faculty for program & event development. May teach a first-year seminar on law-related topics. (5% time)
Direct students toward pre-law high-impact practices including orgs. and clubs such as: Moot Court, Women in the Law, Lawtinx Pre-Law Club, Phi Alpha Delta, and Pre-Law Society. (5% time)

Act as spokesperson and liaison for the program both within the university and with pre-law departments at other universities, with law schools, and other relevant audiences. Organize, host, and/or publicize conferences, workshops, or webinars relevant to the application process, law school, and the legal profession. Serve as the PPAC advising liaison to the Career Center to provide planning support and marketing of the annual Graduate, Professional, and Law School Fair. (5% time)

Partner with Student Affairs, Student Life, Residential Life, Community Outreach and other campus programs to support students who have interest in the field of law. Sustained, informed contact with the Law School Admissions Council (LSAC). Guidance regarding communications to/from the LSAC and LSAT outcomes. Provide outreach to prospective undergraduate students during Orientation, regional campus visits, and recruitment events (i.e. Highlander Day). (5% time)

Maintain assessment data on student applications and admissions in appropriate formats, including electronic. Maintain databases (i.e. Banner, Slate) on pre-law students during their undergraduate and post-graduate stages. Contribute to the professional community (i.e. Pacific Coast Association of Pre-Law Advisors, PLANC-national Pre-Law Association of pre-law advisors at the regional and national level). May build and sustain relationships with regional, statewide and national law organizations (e.g., American Bar Association, Cal Asian Pacific American Bar Association, Phi Alpha Delta, the Hispanic National Bar Association, MALDEF, the Hispanic Bar Association of the Inland Empire, the Riverside County Bar Association, and the Inland Empire Latino Lawyers, among others) that strengthen communities and pathways into the legal profession. (5% time)

Oversee peer advising program for upper-class students to work with first- and second-year students interested in law and, when needed, speak at orientations and recruitment activities. Work with university offices, develop and organize workshops and information sessions on relevant topics, including general admission, applications, letters of recommendation, and strategies for writing personal statements. May supervise support staff, peer mentors, and/or work-study students. (5% time)

Thorough knowledge of advising and counseling techniques. Knowledge of multiple majors, colleges, and schools.
Thorough knowledge of college/school policies, procedures, and requirements.
Skills in judgment and decision-making, problem solving.
Demonstrated understanding of law school admissions landscape.
Abilities in problem identification, reasoning, ability to develop original ideas to solve problems.
Excellent written and oral communication, interpersonal, and counseling skills.
Ability to multi-task.
Knowledge of pre-law student population and UCR student body with a large percentage of first-generation college students.
Thorough knowledge of department/school college policies, procedures, and requirements.
Excellent organizational skills, including the ability to prioritize responsibilities and meet deadlines.
Ability to travel in a professional capacity.
Demonstrated experience with databases, web applications and electronic communications.
Ability to host and participate in programming and events, occasionally on evenings and weekends.
Demonstrated record of commitment to equity in higher education.
